title: Template Syntax & Interpolation 📝
description: Display dynamic data using double curly braces and understand template expressions.

slides.title: The Template – Where Data Meets HTML 🤝
slides.content:
# Angular Templates

An Angular template is HTML with superpowers. It can:

* Show component properties dynamically.
* Bind to element properties (e.g., image `src`).
* Listen to user events (clicks, inputs).
* Render lists and conditionally show/hide elements.

Under the hood, Angular compiles templates into JavaScript that manipulates the DOM efficiently.

slides.title: Interpolation: {{ expression }}
slides.content: Interpolation pulls a value from the component into the view. Just wrap a component property in double curly braces.

slides.title: Interpolation is Not Just Properties 🔢
slides.content:
You can put any valid TypeScript expression inside `{{ }}`:

* Arithmetic: `{{ 2 + 2 }}` → 4
* Method calls: `{{ getName() }}` (though better avoid due to performance)
* Ternary operators: `{{ isLoggedIn ? 'Welcome back' : 'Please sign in' }}`
* Property access: `{{ user.name }}

⚠️ **Important**: The expression must not have side effects (no assignments, no `new`). It must be **idempotent** – running it multiple times produces the same result.

quizData.question: To display a component property `count`, you write {{ _____ }}.
quizData.explanation: You simply put the property name inside the double curly braces.

slides.title: Avoid These in Interpolation ⚠️
slides.content:
## Forbidden Expressions

```html
<!-- ❌ Assignment -->
{{ a = b + 1 }}

<!-- ❌ Increment / Decrement -->
{{ counter++ }}

<!-- ❌ Creating objects -->
{{ new Date() }}
```

These can cause unpredictable behavior or `ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError`.

Stick to simple reads and simple expressions.

slides.title: Displaying Complex Data
slides.content: Interpolation works with objects and arrays too:

quizData.question: You can safely write `{{ count = count + 1 }}` in an Angular template.
quizData.explanation: Assignments are side‑effects and are forbidden in interpolation expressions.
